title: fix(plugin-security): a permission-set assignment is titled by the person's name, not the raw user id
body:
Fixes #24775

Clause-②: no

This PR covers one of the card's two objects, `sys_user_permission_set` (`plugin-security`). The other, `sys_notification_preference` (`service-messaging`), needs a ruling first, so #24775 remains open after this merges. Open choice 1 below gives that ruling's options. Related: #24701 (Record Shares recipient, closed; its seat ruling `6282390889` is the precedent read for this card).

## What changes

`sys_user_permission_set.display_title` is the object's `nameField`. It composed the stored foreign key, `record.user_id + ' → ' + record.permission_set`. So Setup's list of a user's permission sets and the assignment's record page read like `ISu3jHPIrdgD45L1rrC2FuE7DIcsk2ap → qa_fls_rep` (HotCRM pass, F-25).

It now names the person:

```
(isBlank(trim(record.user_id.name)) ? record.user_id.email : record.user_id.name) + ' → ' + record.permission_set
```

- The user's `name`, or their `email` where the name is blank. That is the platform's own `name || email` rule for a person's handle (`auth-manager.ts`, `approval-service.ts`).
- The value is read one hop through `user_id`. That is the formula read path's one-hop traversal (ADR-0079 addendum, 2026-10-18), read under the reader's own authority.
- No stored column, no spec change, no objectui change, no console name mapping.
- `user_id` is read only through the hop. A bare read beside the traversal would be the `traversal-bare-and-traversed` refusal.
- `titleFormat` (`{user_id} → {permission_set}`) is unchanged. It is the rung below the declared pointer in the console's H1 ladder: objectui `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx:2542` at the pin `616df6598b` ("The declared pointer OUTRANKS `titleFormat`"). A renderer reaches it only when the title has no value.
- The field's label and description are unchanged, so no translation bundle moves.

Files:
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`: the expression and its comments.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set-person-title.test.ts` (new): the pins.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-security-assignment-display-title.test.ts`: `sys_user_permission_set` leaves its case table, since the title no longer equals the `titleFormat` text. `sys_user_position` keeps every assertion it had.
- `.changeset/24775-permission-set-assignment-person-title.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security` patch.

## Premises, measured (on `main` at `6b9e6df909`, then merged to `b1676441ba`)

- **H1, holds.** Both objects declare `nameField: 'display_title'`, a text formula with no stored column. The read door serves it: on a real engine (driver-sql, better-sqlite3), `findOne`, a `find` projecting only `display_title`, and the insert response all carry it.
- **H2, read.** `packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts` lists `lookup` and `user` in `TITLE_INELIGIBLE_TYPES`. So the pointer stays on the text formula; no pointer moves.
- **H3.** The console already names the person in a `lookup` column's chip. For the title, though, the platform's server-side resolvers read the title field's value: `resolveRecordDisplayName`, and `servedRecordTitle` in `record-title.ts`. So the person's name has to be in the formula's value. The formula's one hop is the platform's own way to put it there.
- **H4, holds (it was NOT MEASURED in #24701's report).** A formula reads one hop through a reference. This shipped with `d537a318b` and `1bf5f6e17c`, and the ADR-0079 addendum records it. Measured on the real engine with the real `sys_user`, the hop formula gives `Alice Liddell → crm_edit` on the insert response, on `findOne` and on a projected `find`. A grant whose user does not exist reads `null`.
- **`sys_notification_preference` cannot take the same route.** Its `user_id` is `Field.text` (maxLength 255). It holds a `sys_user.id` or the literal `*`, the admin-global default `preference-resolver.ts` reads as `WILDCARD`. The read path serves a hop only through a reference type (`REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`: lookup, master_detail, user, tree, in `field-value.zod.ts`). Measured: a text `user_id` read as `record.user_id.name` gives `null`. See open choice 1.

## Open choice 1: how `sys_notification_preference` can name the person

No route names the person without one of three things: re-typing `user_id`, a stored copy, or a formula-language feature. The dispatch's hard stops forbid the last two in this lane.

- **A. Re-type `user_id` as a `user` reference, and spell the admin-global default as an empty reference instead of `*`.** That is ADR-0118 D1's representation of a non-user in a user column: null, never a sentinel; the display is a render rule. The title then reads the person one hop, as here, and shows the empty reference as the default's label. The Setup form gets a user picker instead of a raw-id text box, and the list column a person chip.
  - Business need: the Setup grid is the measured producer (HotCRM F-25). Zero code producers write `*` rows: `git grep` finds the resolver's constant, its tests and one driver-sql test.
  - Long-term: contract-first. It removes a sentinel from a user column.
  - AI mistakes: a typed reference refuses a non-user id at the write door. Today any string is stored as a "user id" and silently matches nobody.
  - Startup scope: no new column or capability. But it narrows the accept set (`*` and any non-user string refused), so it is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and BREAKING. It owes a stored-row conversion (`*` to null), the resolver change, and a NULL-safe user key part in the unique index (ADR-0120 D3 makes only the organization key part NULL-safe). Effort M, as its own card.
- **B. A console display rule for the column only** (a widget hint on `user_id`). No such widget exists at the pin. The shipped hints are `recipient-picker`, `object-ref`, `position-ref`, `permission-ref` and `filter-condition`. And a hint on `user_id` cannot reach the composite title, so the H1 and the list's title column stay raw. It does not close the finding.
- **C. A stored name column:** refused by the dispatch (it goes stale on rename).
- **D. A by-id lookup function over a text column:** the spec and formula lane's. It would be a second traversal dialect beside the one-hop rule.
- **Recommendation: A, as its own `service-messaging` card.** The long-term and AI-safety axes both favour typing the column. The cost is a breaking narrowing with a data conversion, and that is the maintainer's to rule.

## Open choice 2: the hop costs a read on every authenticated request of a grant holder

The authorization prelude reads the caller's grants with no field projection: `tryFind(ql, 'sys_user_permission_set', { user_id: userId }, 100)` in `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:1457`. A read with no projection computes every formula, so `display_title`'s hop now costs one batched `sys_user` read there.

Measured with `auth-prelude-query-count.pin.test.ts`'s own rig (real engine, real `AuthManager`, `resolveAuthzContext`), old formula against new. The probe was a scratch file and is not committed:

| principal | old formula | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no direct grant | 8 reads, 4 round trips | 8 reads, 4 round trips |
| one direct grant | 8 reads, 4 round trips | 9 reads, 5 round trips (`sys_user` 2 to 3) |

The committed pin measures a principal with no direct grant, so it stays green and cannot see this. The grants cache that would amortise it is off by default (`OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS=0`). Other reads of the table that name no projection pay the same single read per page: the explain engine, the platform-admin scan, the last-admin guard and the auth manager's grant reads. They are admin-time or boot-time paths.

- **A. Land as is.** Every request of an organization admin or platform admin pays one more indexed read and one more round trip, for a title nobody on that path reads.
- **B. Land after (or with) a `core`-lane change that projects the prelude's grant read to the columns the resolver reads,** plus a grant-holder case in the prelude pin. The title is still declared once, on the object, and the hot path reads only what it uses. Which columns the resolver reads is that lane's to measure. A wrong projection would drop a column a security decision reads.
- **C. Withdraw the hop.** The title stays the raw id.
- **Recommendation: B.**
  - Business need: the title serves Setup pages, while the cost lands on every request.
  - Long-term: B avoids a hidden coupling, where a display formula costs authorization a round trip.
  - AI mistakes: the extended pin makes the next such cost visible.
  - Startup scope: one projection and one pin case, and no new gate.

## Tests (head `2deb9e32e6`; every run under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, exit read from its `VERDICT` line)

- Closure: `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/plugin-security^...' --filter '@objectstack/service-messaging^...' build` gave `VERDICT command-exit 0`. Then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security build` gave `VERDICT command-exit 0`; `check-dts-emitted`: 1/1, and `dist/index.mjs` carries the new expression (count 1).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (whole package, code tree of `07c9bf2315`): `Test Files 196 passed (196)`, `Tests 4049 passed | 45 skipped (4094)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` (on `2deb9e32e6`'s tree): `VERDICT command-exit 0`. It includes `check:test-typecheck: OK`, whose `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*`, the new pin file among them.
- The two title files on `2deb9e32e6`'s tree: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 14 passed (14)` (8 in the new file, 6 for `sys_user_position`).
- The new pins, with real `sys_user` and the real assignment definition on driver-sql:
  - the registered pointer, and the formula reads `permission_set`, `user_id.email` and `user_id.name`, nothing bare;
  - the person's name on the insert response, on `findOne` and on a `find` projecting only `display_title`. `resolveRecordDisplayName` and `servedRecordTitle` agree, and the row still holds the foreign key;
  - the control: a user whose stored name is empty, or only spaces, is titled by their email;
  - read as the reader, under a `sys_user` row-scope middleware in the shape the security plugin composes:
    - a readable user is named;
    - an unreadable one leaves the title `null`, and neither the name nor the email appears in the served row;
    - SYSTEM reads the name;
    - a missing user reads `null`;
  - the write door refuses a row missing either title column;
  - no stored column and no search companion.
- `sys_notification_preference` is untouched, so no `service-messaging` test or typecheck is owed.

## Ablation (one leg: the one pinned behaviour this PR changes)

- The mutation: `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the new expression with the old one, inside a script carrying `trap 'git checkout HEAD -- "$ABS"' EXIT INT TERM` over an absolute path.
- Proof it landed on disk: anchor count 1 to 0, replacement count 0 to 1, blob `72b5b4afc1` to `712f8d6419`.
- The subject is imported from `src/` by a relative path, so no `dist/` was involved.
- Mutated run of `sys-user-permission-set-person-title.test.ts`: `Tests 6 failed | 2 passed (8)`. That is the expected direction, red. The two still green pin unchanged behaviour: the missing-column refusal and no stored column.
- Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- "$ABS"`: blob after restore `72b5b4afc1`, equal to HEAD's blob; `git diff HEAD` empty; `git status --porcelain` empty.

## Acceptance notes

- Same family, not in this card's file surface. The seat should fold these into the family's close-out card, not file single cards:
  - `sys_user_position.display_title` (`record.user_id + ' → ' + record.position`, `sys-user-position.object.ts:76`). `user_id` is a lookup there, so this PR's route applies. It is pinned today, on the engine read door, as `usr_alice → sales_manager`.
  - `sys_notification_delivery` (`record.channel + ' → ' + record.recipient_id`) and `sys_notification_subscription` (`record.principal + ' · ' + record.topic`). Both are text columns, so they share open choice 1's fork.
- The prelude pin's blind spot (a principal with no direct grant) is open choice 2's. Noted, not filed.

## Round 2 (head `66a590fd88`)

**Merge.** `origin/main` at `865d2c8cf4` is merged in as `9474db510e`, with no rebase and no force-push. It brings #24941 (`644e4b2c54`): the authz prelude's grant read now names `permission_set`, `organization_id`, `valid_from` and `valid_until`. Git reported no conflict and no `os-regen` deferral.

**One semantic conflict, settled in one line** (`894860ed7a`). #24941's pin, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-prelude-query-count.pin.test.ts`, has a pair of direct-grant cases: "as declared" and "with a title that reads one hop through user_id". Before it counts anything, the "as declared" case checks the value of the declared title, and it expected the raw user id. On this branch the declared title is the person-named one. So on the merge commit that check read `Prelude → prelude_editor`, and the case went red (`Expected: "USER_ID → prelude_editor"`, `Received: "Prelude → prelude_editor"`). The count assertions after it never ran. The line now expects `Prelude → prelude_editor` in both cases. No count, rig or other assertion changed.

**One sentence the merge made false** (`66a590fd88`). The changeset's Cost bullet said the prelude rises to 9 reads in 5 round trips for a grant holder. It now says the prelude's grant read names its columns, so it computes no title and stays at 8 reads in 4 round trips. The rest of the changeset is unchanged.

**The prelude, re-measured on the merged tree.** This uses this PR's real `sys_user_permission_set` definition, on the rig of the pin above, by round 1's method. The probe was a scratch file, deleted and never committed.

| read, for a principal holding one direct grant | reads | round trips |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the prelude (`resolveAuthzContext`), round 1 on `b1676441ba` | 9 | 5 |
| the prelude (`resolveAuthzContext`), now | 8 | 4 |
| control: the same grant read, no projection | 2 (`sys_user_permission_set` 1, `sys_user` 1) | 2 |
| control: the same grant read, projected to the four columns | 1 | 1 |

- The prelude's reads match the pin's `PRELUDE_READS` exactly: `sys_session` 1, `sys_user` 2, `sys_member` 2, `sys_user_position` 1, `sys_user_permission_set` 1, `sys_metadata_activation` 1.
- The unprojected control returns `Prelude → prelude_editor`. So the hop is live on this engine, and the instrument counts it. The projected control returns exactly the four columns.
- So on `main` now, the hop adds no read and no round trip to the prelude.
- After the one-line change, the pin passes on the merged tree: all 7 cases, both direct-grant cases at 8 reads in 4 round trips.

**Tests on `66a590fd88`.** Every run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, and each exit is read from its VERDICT line.
